title: Kulajda
description: A soured cream soup of potato, mushroom, and a great deal of dill, with a poached egg dropped into each bowl. It should taste sour first and sweet a moment later — that balance is the whole dish.
notes: Cut the dill stems in with the fronds. They carry more of the flavour and they soften completely in the pot.

ingredients.name: mushrooms
ingredients.note: sliced; wild ones if you have them

ingredients.name: eggs
ingredients.note: as fresh as you can get

steps.text: Simmer the potatoes with the bay leaf, caraway seeds, and salt in the vegetable stock until a cube is just short of tender.
Add the sliced mushrooms and cook until they darken and sink.
Whisk the plain flour into the sour cream until there is not a lump left, then slacken it with a ladleful of the hot broth.
steps.tip: Tempering is the whole trick. Cold cream straight into a simmering pot splits into curds and no amount of whisking gathers it back.

steps.text: Stir the slackened cream into the pot and hold it just below a simmer — it must not boil again.
Fish out the bay leaf, then season with the white wine vinegar, sugar, and black pepper, adding the vinegar a spoon at a time.
steps.tip: Aim for sour on the front of the tongue and sweet behind it. If it lands flat, it is almost always short of vinegar rather than salt.

steps.text: Poach the eggs in a separate pan of barely trembling water.
Stir most of the dill into the pot, ladle out, slide an egg into each bowl, and scatter the rest of the dill over.
